scope: Actual production Core QueuedMedia/VideoRepair plus CoreVideoEgress, persistent target RTP mapping and guarded source-clock IO through local ICE/DTLS/SRTP/SRTCP peers. Policy/relationships/capture and port-cleanup adapters are isolated fixtures. No Store/canonical video host, decoded-picture/browser/full-fallback qualification.
implementation: CoreVideoEgress validates one exact VP8/90000 video or screen port and physical track before consuming its queue. Queue/sequence waits hold no permission reader. The original owned write invokes QueuedMedia::deliver_video_with_repair inside the actual RTC driver; only successful original IO returns an opaque Core repair handle.

Every explicit NACK repair calls VideoRepair::repair, reacquiring current source/target/audience, route generation, gate and explicit selection permissions. The original full RTP is disclosed only within those guards; its original target SSRC/PT/sequence/timestamp mapping is reconstructed, then driver fact equality and current negotiated identity checks apply. Repair never advances the primary timeline or replaces the current sender-clock mapping.

TrackLocalStaticRTP now owns one typed timeline per actual primary SSRC, shared even by cloned track handles. Unknown SSRCs and competing state types refuse. Metadata persists through expired repair producers, egress drop/rebind and source replacement, and is released with the physical track. It holds no policy reader, Core controller or packet payload.

Target mapping preserves source fragment timestamps, sequence loss gaps and wrapping arithmetic. Duplicate/older source packets and backward timestamps refuse. A new original Core source generation or SSRC starts at the next target sequence/tick; the same constant timestamp offset is applied to its source-clock metadata. Explicit repair reuses its original mapping.

Owned RTP IO can carry source timing. The driver checks the exact SenderClockHandle installed by its reviewed physical peer profile, repeats source lifetime immediately before actual UDP, and commits timing only after successful primary socket submission. Repair checks lifetime without applying an older source mapping. Unreviewed wrappers do not inherit clock ownership.

Core native/local None clock provenance retains native timing. Some provenance without an authoritative anchor stays pending, and retired predicates refuse IO. Clock metadata is never authorization. Core original age and the driver one-use deadline still bound pending IO, whose destruction precedes permission release. Canonical video host/controller/cleanup installation remains required.

behavior: Core source RTP with SSRC3333/PT95 is delivered and repaired as the exact negotiated target SSRC1111/PT96, over actual encrypted packets, with negotiated RTX, no RTX and declined RTX answers. Loss uses a successful real UDP submission to a designated local discard sink, then explicit encrypted SRTCP NACK.

Current source and recipient revocation and private-audience withdrawal refuse repairs with no native cached send. Restoration plus a new explicit NACK succeeds on the same peer. No idle Core policy reader remains.
Clearing/reselecting explicit video subscriptions and pausing/resuming the original source invalidate old repair handles. The repaired packet cannot inherit a new selection or gate generation.

An actual pending repair socket retains both Core policy leases. Original expiry drops the socket future while both leases are still live, then releases them; releasing the old socket gate later emits no late packet. Cancelling a pending original yields OutcomeUnknown, drains original IO and creates no repair handle; subsequent authorized video succeeds.

After every old repair producer expires and the egress is dropped, replacement source and target Core ports reuse the same physical track timeline. Input source seq5/timestamp15000 maps to target seq12/timestamp33001 after original seq11/timestamp33000; an explicit NACK12 repairs that exact target mapping, without reallocation.

Retired source-clock provenance refuses both original and retained repair IO. A later current source frame succeeds. A different connected peer clock, despite the same negotiated primary SSRC, cannot write or retime this sender. Both peers remain separately owned and close.
